cards.title: SNAP / Food Stamps
cards.notes: Provides food benefits to low-income individuals and families.

cards.title: Greater Chicago Food Depository
cards.notes: Provides food assistance through a network of partner agencies, pantries, and hot meal programs.

cards.title: Illinois Food Bank Association — Statewide Network
cards.notes: A network of 9 regional food banks and over 2,000 partner agencies serving all 102 Illinois counties.

cards.title: TANF Cash Assistance (Illinois DHS — TCA)
cards.notes: Provides cash assistance to families with children.

cards.title: WIC (Illinois WIC Program)
cards.notes: Provides food benefits, nutrition counseling, breastfeeding support, and referrals for pregnant women, postpartum women, infants, and children under 5.

cards.title: Illinois Medicaid / Medicaid Expansion
cards.notes: Provides healthcare coverage to low-income adults, families, children, pregnant women, seniors, and individuals with disabilities.

cards.title: Cook County Health (CCH) — Stroger Hospital + CountyCare
cards.notes: Public hospital system for Cook County residents, including a Level 1 trauma center and a Medicaid managed care plan.

cards.title: Chicago Department of Public Health (CDPH) — City Clinics
cards.notes: Provides sliding scale primary care, sexual health, mental health, substance use, and maternal health services to Chicago residents.

cards.title: Illinois Immigrant Health Connect (State-Funded)
cards.notes: State-funded healthcare coverage for undocumented immigrants age 42+.

cards.title: Federally Qualified Health Centers — Illinois Network
cards.notes: Provides sliding scale primary, dental, and behavioral health services regardless of insurance status or ability to pay.

cards.title: Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) — Emergency Rental Assistance
cards.notes: Administers state-level rental assistance programs for low-income renters facing eviction or housing instability.

cards.title: Chicago RLTO Tenant Hotline — Metropolitan Tenants Organization (MTO)
cards.notes: Provides free tenant rights counseling, habitability complaints, security deposit disputes, and eviction defense for Chicago renters covered by the RLTO.

cards.title: LIHEAP / IHWAP (Illinois Home Weatherization & Energy Assistance)
cards.notes: Provides heating, cooling, crisis utility shutoff prevention, and weatherization assistance.

cards.title: ComEd Low Income Programs
cards.notes: Provides rate reduction and deferred payment plans for low-income electric customers.

cards.title: Illinois Legal Aid Online (ILAO) — Statewide Self-Help
cards.notes: Provides free legal information, court forms, and self-help guides for housing, family, benefits, and consumer issues.

cards.title: Legal Aid Chicago (formerly LAF)
cards.notes: Provides legal assistance in housing, family, benefits, DV, immigration, and consumer matters.

cards.title: Prairie State Legal Services — Downstate + Suburban
cards.notes: Provides legal assistance in housing, family, benefits, DV, elder, and immigration matters.

cards.title: Land of Lincoln Legal Aid — Southern Illinois
cards.notes: Provides legal assistance in housing, family, benefits, DV, elder, and consumer matters.

cards.title: Illinois Domestic Violence Hotline
cards.notes: Provides 24/7 crisis support, shelter referral, and safety planning for domestic violence survivors.

cards.title: Chicago Domestic Violence Help Line
cards.notes: Provides 24/7 crisis support, shelter, legal advocacy, and a City Hall Domestic Violence Help Desk for Chicago DV survivors.

cards.title: Equip for Equality — Disability Rights Illinois
cards.notes: Provides legal representation and advocacy for people with disabilities on issues such as ADA, Section 504, abuse/neglect, special education, and healthcare rights.

cards.title: Illinois Unemployment Insurance (IDES)
cards.notes: Provides temporary income to workers who have lost their job through no fault of their own.

cards.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
cards.summary: Call or text 988 for immediate mental health crisis support. Free, confidential, 24/7. Trained counselors can help with suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, substance use, and mental health crises. Also available via chat at 988lifeline.org.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing a mental health crisis, suicidal thoughts, or emotional distress.
cards.how_to_access: Call or text 988. Chat at 988lifeline.org. For veterans, press 1 after dialing 988.

cards.title: NAMI Helpline & Support Groups
cards.summary: National Alliance on Mental Illness provides free peer support, education, and advocacy. NAMI HelpLine: 1-800-950-NAMI (6264). Family-to-Family program helps families understand mental health conditions and navigate the system.
cards.who_qualifies: Individuals with mental health conditions and their family members.
cards.how_to_access: Call 1-800-950-NAMI or text 'HELPLINE' to 62640. Find local NAMI affiliate at nami.org/find-support.

cards.title: Protection & Advocacy Organization
cards.summary: Every state has a federally mandated Protection & Advocacy (P&A) organization with legal authority to investigate abuse and neglect in psychiatric facilities. P&A organizations can enter any facility, access records, and file lawsuits. This is often the most powerful tool available for people harmed in the mental health system.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone with a disability who has experienced abuse, neglect, or rights violations in a facility.
cards.how_to_access: Find your state P&A at ndrn.org/about/ndrn-member-agencies/ or call the NDRN at 202-408-9514.

cards.title: Know Your Rights: Illinois Emergency Admission
cards.summary: If you are placed on an involuntary hold in IL, you have rights: the initial hold cannot exceed 24 hours without a court hearing. You have the right to an attorney at the hearing. You have the right to present evidence and call witnesses. You have the right to an independent psychiatric evaluation. You can challenge the hold at any time.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone placed on an involuntary psychiatric hold or facing commitment proceedings.
cards.how_to_access: Request to speak with the patient advocate. Ask for a copy of your patient rights. Contact your state's Protection & Advocacy organization.

cards.title: Your Right to Your Psychiatric Records
cards.summary: Under HIPAA (45 CFR § 164.524), you have the right to access your complete medical record, including psychiatric treatment records. The facility must respond within 30 days. If they deny access, you can file a complaint with HHS Office for Civil Rights. Under HIPAA § 164.526, you also have the right to request amendments to inaccurate records.
cards.who_qualifies: Any current or former psychiatric patient.
cards.how_to_access: Submit a written request to the facility's Health Information Management department. If denied, file complaint at hhs.gov/ocr.

cards.title: SAMHSA National Helpline
cards.summary: Free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referral and information service for mental health and substance use disorders. Available in English and Spanish. Provides referrals to local treatment facilities, support groups, and community-based organizations.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone seeking mental health or substance use treatment information and referrals.
